# Generated failures and endpoint classes point back to the Phrase source
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #161, sha256:8cccc0e48444505eda58977bb2a80a6391d321e1030d3e43de82545669c75c36). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; from the Usable v1 retro product feedback)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Product feedback gathered from Codex and Grok at the Usable v1 retro, 2026-10-28 (docs/retros/usable-v1-2026-10-28.md): the demo's real rules, validation, storing and updating, all sit in native C#, so a cold model has to learn generated C# conventions to change them and a reader of the Phrase cannot see the rule.
- **Depends on:** 138
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want any failure of a generated API to be traceable to its Phrase endpoint, step and spec through a source map and a trace command, so that I can find the spec without reading the generated C# and without the running API exposing source details.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the Tasks demo, When phrase build runs, Then a separate source map file is written next to the generated projects in the same build step (fields: schema version, build id, kind, name, Phrase file base name and line, owning endpoint and step, spec line range, generated C# file, method and file hash), the generated C# contains no Phrase endpoint, step or source-line knowledge (no X-Phrase-Source header, no // phrase: comments, no source file name), and the build id is also compiled into the generated assembly
  2. Given the map, When phrase trace EmptyTitle (or TitleTooLong, NotFound, StoreUnavailable, or a Class.Method frame) runs, Then it prints the failure, the Phrase line, the spec lines, the generated C# location and the build check, exits nonzero for an unknown name, and warns or refuses when the map build id does not match the assembly; the live HTTP test runner reads the map and asserts it for every declared failure of the demo
  3. Given the generated API and the publish output, When they are inspected, Then the API serves no path to the map, the map is excluded from publish output, the 422 response bodies and the 11 specs are unchanged, the README drift test and the Usable v1 bars stay green, and the same source gives the same output on Windows and Linux (base name only, LF line counting)

## Context

- A reader the personas may miss: the engineer on call who must trace a production failure back through generated code (found at the Usable v1 retro). Prefer the smallest change that makes the trace possible.

- Decision D111 (2026-10-28, supersedes D110): traceability is a source map outside the runtime, not knowledge inside the generated C#. The header, its switch and the // phrase: comments were reverted (commit 1b287f3). #line directives are a separate card.
